Part 3 begins with the reproduction of one of three recorded results, chosen by you. The three reproduced models are three estimators, and they lead into what a panel of 27 countries needs from its methods: fixed effects against random intercepts, the within–between model, and a test that copes with few clusters. Then the menu is taken apart decision by decision, and the part ends with a round of exploration of your own. The part takes ninety minutes.

## 1. The instruction of Multi100

**On the slides.** The slides read the four instructions of the second Multi100 task word for word and say what each of them assumes. The slides then show the columns of the panel and the three analyses that can be reproduced on aggregate data, and make you analyst no. 6.

## 2. Task 3 – The reproduction

[Open the browser lab at Task 3](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-3-reproduction){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

Choose one analyst and run its cells in order; each cell with gaps to fill has a hint and a full solution under it. For 018OL, one cell installs two packages, a download of about 32 MB. Type the analyst and the value in the chat, for example `018OL t = -1.206`, hold it, and send it when the facilitator says go. If you work in the workspace, use the working script instead.

| Analyst | Data | Model | Recorded by Multi100 |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| C6HJR | the course panel, `EUframes_cy.csv`, 270 country-years | fixed effects for country and year, conventional standard errors | t = −3.804 on 233 df |
| KQXUE | `analyst_KQXUE.csv`, 270 country-years | a fixed effect for each country, conventional standard errors | t = −7.169 on 242 df |
| 018OL | `analyst_018OL.csv`, 420 cells of country, year and wave | random intercepts for country, year and wave, Satterthwaite degrees of freedom | t = −1.206 on 396.9 df |

## 3. The three models and few clusters

**On the slides.** The slides explain why everyone with the same analyst got the same t while the three analysts did not, and set the three reproduced models side by side: two-way and country fixed effects against random intercepts. The slides then present the within–between model, and conventional, clustered and CR2 errors with Satterthwaite degrees of freedom on the same estimate.

To go further: [The statistical methods behind the course](../../companion/stats-methods.qmd#sec-pooled), sections 3 to 5.

## 4. The specification menu

**On the slides**, with the specification menu open in another tab.

[Open the specification menu](../../cases/eu-frames/menu.qmd){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

The slides take you through the fourteen decisions, the three groups into which they sort, the options that the curve of 864 keeps and what Task 2 of Multi100 left open. The slides end on the ground rules for the menu and on the convention of claim alignment. Every decision starts from the reproduced specification, the model of C6HJR, whichever analyst you reproduced.

## 5. The methods behind the menu

**On the slides.** A methodological tutorial takes nine of the fourteen decisions, a slide or two each. It covers the six framing scales, building a scale from a mean, a sum or a share, claim alignment and a bounded scale in a linear model, then the predictor and its form. It goes on to the estimators for countries and years and what fixed effects adjust for, the copredictor, sample restrictions and weights, and ends on making the axes comparable.

## 6. Task 4 – The menu

[Open the browser lab at Task 4](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd#task-4-explore){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"}

If you work in the workspace, use your report or the working script instead. Call `try_spec()` three or four times, changing one argument at a time, and print the tries side by side with `my_experiments()`. Then submit the one that you would defend with `submit_exploration()`. Your dot is drawn on the class chart of the [Multiverse page](../../cases/eu-frames/multiverse.qmd#class-results) as an exploratory result.

**By the end of the part** you have reproduced a recorded result, you can say what fixed effects, random intercepts and the CR2 test each do on this panel and what each decision of the menu does to an estimate, and you have an exploratory dot on the class chart.
